title: Punt 3PTM: Player Targets
markdown:
**Summary.** Punting 3PTM costs less in our league than rankings suggest. Two threes a game is now only average, and threes are easy to stream off waivers. Build around non-shooters who add FG%, REB, BLK and steals, such as Amen Thompson, Jalen Duren, Dyson Daniels and Ausar Thompson, then fill the end of the auction with cheap centers at 1 to 3 USD.

## Why non-shooters lose less here

Two experts say the same thing: threes are easy to find on waivers. Do not overpay for three-point specialists at the auction. A player who makes no threes gives up less real value than his ranking shows, because you can stream threes back if you need them. ([10-03](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1214), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1512), [07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=636))

The bar for threes has also gone up. About two threes a game is now average in fantasy. A shooter who only hits two is nothing special. On 2026-10-18, do not pay extra for a player whose main selling point is two threes a game. Spend that money on FG%, REB, BLK and steals instead. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=569), [09-28](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1744))

What this means in our league: when you rank players for a punt 3PTM team, treat zero threes as a small cost, not a big one. If you decide not to fully punt, our daily FAB waivers and the cap of 6 adds per week give you room to stream a shooter in weeks where you are close in threes. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=636), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1512))

## The limits of the build

There is a tension in the notes. One side says non-shooters are barely hurt, because threes are easy to stream. The other side warns that a big-man build is harder to run than it looks. Only REB, BLK and FG% move together, and threes and FG% pull against each other, so adding threes back to a big-man core is hard. Both points hold. Punting threes is cheap, but stacking only centers leaves you weak in AST, ST and FT%. Mix in guards and wings who add steals and assists without threes. ([07-07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=636), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=819), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1031))

Check FT% on every target. Gobert, Claxton, Ausar Thompson and Mitchell Robinson shoot poorly from the line. They suit a team that punts both 3PTM and FT%. Hartenstein, Zubac and Murray-Boyles take so few free throws that the damage is small. ([Rudy Gobert](#player/196), [Nic Claxton](#player/105), [Ausar Thompson](#player/549), [Mitchell Robinson](#player/486), [Isaiah Hartenstein](#player/226), [Ivica Zubac](#player/620), [Collin Murray-Boyles](#player/403))

## Core targets

Amen Thompson is the best guard fit. He makes about 0.3 threes a game but gives a 54% FG from a guard slot, 7.7 rebounds, 1.6 steals and blocks. His profile says a price near the Yahoo range of about 25 to 35 USD is safer than the ESPN price. In the first weeks, check that his blocks return near 0.9 and his FG% reaches 55%. ([Amen Thompson](#player/548))

Jalen Duren is the FG% and rebounds anchor, with about 19 to 20 points and no threes. His profile says bid up to about 20 USD and let others go higher. Dyson Daniels is a steals anchor (projected 2.2 a game) who also adds rebounds, assists and FG%, with a fair range of 10 to 18 USD. Ausar Thompson adds elite steals plus good FG%, rebounds and blocks, and the experts call him a steal who should go clearly higher than his market price. ([Jalen Duren](#player/154), [Dyson Daniels](#player/128), [Ausar Thompson](#player/549))

For a second center, Jarrett Allen and Ivica Zubac are both FG% and rebounds anchors. For Allen, stop around 10 to 13 USD. For Zubac, his Yahoo average cost of about 8 USD is the fair price. Indiana's 3-4-3 playoff schedule is a minus for Zubac. ([Jarrett Allen](#player/14), [Ivica Zubac](#player/620))

## Mid-price bigs with a catch

Rudy Gobert gives about 11 rebounds, 1.6 blocks and 67% FG. His 52.6% FT makes him a strong buy only if you also punt FT%. His fair range is 5 to 10 USD. Minnesota has a two-game week in playoff week 20. ([Rudy Gobert](#player/196))

Zach Edey is a strong FG%, REB and BLK piece for a team that can also punt TO. The experts call him top 60 at worst. A price in the high single digits to low teens is reasonable if you accept the ankle risk. Zion Williamson brings strong FG% and 22 to 23 points with no threes. Aim for about 12 USD or less, and watch how often he rests on back-to-backs. ([Zach Edey](#player/158), [Zion Williamson](#player/612))

## End-of-auction flyers at 1 to 3 USD

The last rounds are full of cheap centers who add FG% and blocks with no threes: Claxton, Queta, Gafford, Poeltl, Missi, Diabaté and Isaiah Jackson. Their profiles price most of them at 1 to 3 USD. Each one depends on winning the starting job or the minutes, so check his role in the first weeks and drop him fast if it does not hold. ([Nic Claxton](#player/105), [Neemias Queta](#player/467), [Daniel Gafford](#player/183), [Jakob Poeltl](#player/447), [Yves Missi](#player/387), [Moussa Diabaté](#player/138), [Isaiah Jackson](#player/262))

For more than FG% and blocks, target Hartenstein (rebounds, assists, steals, 61% FG), Sharpe (rebounds, steals, FG%) and Murray-Boyles (58% FG, blocks, steals, few turnovers). The experts see top 100 value in all three, with more upside if their minutes rise. ([Isaiah Hartenstein](#player/226), [Day'Ron Sharpe](#player/509), [Collin Murray-Boyles](#player/403))

Some cheap non-shooters at guard and wing cover the categories big men miss: Porter for steals and assists, Tre Jones for assists and a guard's FG%, Jaquez for FG%, assists and rebounds, and Lendeborg and Queen for rebounds, assists, steals and blocks. DeRozan fits a punt 3PTM team for points, FT% and low turnovers, but not for FG%, REB or BLK. The sites disagree on Jaquez: Yahoo projects 54.2% FG and ESPN 50.2%. ([Kevin Porter Jr.](#player/450), [Tre Jones](#player/295), [Jaime Jaquez Jr.](#player/271), [Yaxel Lendeborg](#player/330), [Derik Queen](#player/466), [DeMar DeRozan](#player/135))

## Waiver watch list

These players should not be bought on 2026-10-18. Track them for FAB claims instead. Paul Reed becomes a must-add if Duren misses time. Ayton is a quick add if Anthony Davis gets hurt. Beringer handcuffs Gobert. Kalkbrenner matters only if Diabaté loses the job. ([Paul Reed](#player/474), [Deandre Ayton](#player/24), [Joan Beringer](#player/41), [Ryan Kalkbrenner](#player/301))

Some players are later-season adds aimed at our playoffs (weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28). Lively is out until around Thanksgiving, and Dallas has a 4-4-4 playoff schedule. Konan Niederhäuser is a free pickup to hold in an IL slot, with a good 4-3-4 playoff schedule. Mark Williams may return in mid to late March. Butler is at most a 1 USD IL stash if you have a spare slot. ([Dereck Lively II](#player/335), [Yanic Konan Niederhäuser](#player/417), [Mark Williams](#player/608), [Jimmy Butler III](#player/78))
